fields.subnational_unit: Portage County, Ohio (Portage County Health District)
fields.population: onsite wastewater treatment systems (OWTS) found faulty by Board of Health inspections, January 2015 to June 2023, and the households responsible for correcting them after a Notice of Violation (NOV)
fields.sample_size: 1,270 OWTS met inclusion criteria for description; 203 functioning, 1,021 failed systems analysed descriptively (487 point-of-sale [POS], 534 non-POS); 938 complete cases in the logistic regression models
fields.effect_measure: odds ratio of correcting a defective OWTS within the 120-day NOV deadline, point-of-sale inspection versus non-POS inspection (annual, nuisance-complaint, newly installed, stormwater IDDE)
fields.effect_estimate: Unadjusted logistic model: odds of compliance within 120 days were more than seven times higher for POS inspections (OR 7.225, 95% CI 5.389-9.686, p < 0.0001). Adjusted model (OWTS type, correction type, cost, age) described in the methods; its result lay beyond the part of the text the Drive reader returned and was not seen.
fields.adjusted_or_unadjusted: unadjusted OR extracted; adjusted OR not seen (text truncated)
fields.covariates: type of new OWTS (traditional, alternative, sewer connection), type of correction (replacement, repair), correction cost per $1,000, age of system in 10-year units (adjusted model)
fields.model_type: unadjusted and adjusted logistic regression (SAS) with ArcGIS mapping; retrospective non-experimental design on administrative inspection records
fields.study_design: retrospective cross-sectional analysis of local health-district administrative records (non-experimental), PhD dissertation
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: Low concern (appraised 2026-10-04 on the full text, partly read; supersedes the sparse-extraction 'High concern' of 2026-09-28; JBI Cross Sectional items 1-8: Yes,Yes,Yes,Yes,Yes,Yes,Yes,Yes; 8/8 Yes). Basis: inclusion criteria by date, complete data and failed-system status; setting described (county health district); POS vs non-POS context recorded in the district database; objective 120-day NOV deadline; four named confounders adjusted for; logistic regression with ORs and CIs. Caveats: single county, administrative records, the adjusted results and discussion were not read, and POS is a self-selected pathway (sales trigger the inspection).
fields.section: Full text (dissertation, Ch.1-4): Research Question and Hypothesis; Methods and variables; Descriptive and unadjusted logistic results
fields.exact_location: Research question p8; Methods p30-31; sample flow p40-41 (Figure 4); variables and model equations p44-49; results p54-59 (unadjusted OR p59)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a retrospective cross-sectional analysis (PhD dissertation) of Portage County, Ohio, inspection records read in full text 2026-10-04 (partly: the Drive reader truncated the document). Point-of-sale inspection triggered by real-estate transfer is associated with far higher odds of correcting faulty onsite sewage systems within the 120-day notice (unadjusted OR 7.2, CI 5.4-9.7); adjusted results not seen. A single county, administrative data, self-selected pathway.
